alt: A Local Property Tax letter in the letterbox of a dark front door, above a sunny street of red brick houses with a church spire behind.
lead: Local Property Tax is a yearly tax on homes in Ireland, collected by Revenue. As a new owner you will pay it, but when you start depends on the date you bought.

sections.title: When you become liable
body: You pay LPT for a year if you own the home on 1 November of the year before. If you buy on 15 October 2026, you pay LPT for 2027. If you buy on 15 November 2026, the seller owned the home on 1 November, so the 2027 tax is theirs and yours starts in 2028.
Your solicitor checks that the seller's LPT is paid up to date, because unpaid LPT stays with the property.

sections.title: How the tax is worked out
body: You value your own home, and the value places it in a band. For 2026 to 2030 the values are based on 1 November 2025. The bands were widened by 20%, so that price rises alone move fewer homes into a higher band.

head: Value on 1 November 2025
LPT a year
rows: Rises with each band; see Revenue's table

body: Local authorities can raise or lower the basic rate by up to 15%, so the amount varies a little between counties.

sections.title: Valuing a new home
body: If your home is newly built, ask Revenue how the valuation date applies to it. For any home, Revenue's LPT guidance helps you estimate a value from sales of similar homes.

sections.title: Paying it
body: Register the property and file your return in Revenue's myAccount.
Choose how to pay: deduction from your salary or pension, direct debit, a single payment by card, or through a payment service provider.
Deduction from your salary spreads the tax evenly over the year, which many new owners find easiest.
My journey keeps this on your settling-in list at step 27.

body.tip: Keep a note of how you reached your valuation, such as the sold prices of similar homes. Revenue can ask for it later.

journey: Step 27 of My journey, Register for Local Property Tax, sits in the settling-in phase, next to the other first tasks in your new home.
